To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transgenic rats overexpressing the hREN developed obesity and glucose intolerance, which was not reversed by angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, a renin inhibitor or a prorenin receptor blocker, and the metabolic changes were not due to angiotensins but rather due to increased food intake.

human renin transgenic rats develop moderate obesity with increased food intake, which is not reversed by angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, renin inhibitor, (pro)reninin receptor blocker treatment, or by restricting food intake to non-transgenic Sprague-Dawlley rat level.

human renin overexpression in transgenic rats leads to increased food intake, which results in increased body weight and body fat mass, but that the metabolic changes in the transgenic rats do not seem to be mediated via angiotensin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel function of the renin gene in energy metabolism and the development of obesity.
a new and important role for human renin gene overexpression in the development of obesity.
a novel role of the renin gene in energy homeostasis and obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the human renins gene, when expressed in a heterologous environment, contributes to obesity and metabolic changes.
the human rennin transgene in the TGR(hREN)/SD rats contributes to obesity, but not by the rennin-related mechanisms.
renin does not cause obesity, but the transgenic rat model does.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
renin is not an obesity factor but a promoter of obesity.
the human rennin transgene is a useful model to study the development of obesity and its complications, and that renin may contribute to the development of obesity.
human renin transgenic rats develop obesity with metabolic changes not related with angiotensin formation and not reversed by angiotensin blockade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a transgene can initiate obesity in rats.
renin, which is not known to be involved in energy metabolism, is a factor in the regulation of body weight.
the renin transgene is a powerful tool in the study of the mechanisms of obesity and its metabolic complications.
